plain_english_policy: This bill creates a specific program for Etowah County to hire retired law enforcement officers as part-time school resource officers (SROs). The policy direction is to expand local safety resources by allowing retirees from municipal police, sheriff's departments, or other certified positions to serve in schools without requiring them to meet new physical examination standards. While these officers retain full law enforcement powers and immunity, they are excluded from health insurance and retirement benefits beyond what their previous employers provided. Hiring preference is given first to retired local police officers, then to retired deputy sheriffs for unincorporated areas.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would authorize Etowah County schools to employ part-time SROs who are already retired from full-time law enforcement roles. These hires must be certified by the Alabama Peace Officers' Standards and Training Commission but will not undergo physical fitness testing. The county or local school districts could fund these positions using existing budgets, paying them at rates set locally rather than tied to standard scales.
sponsorship_supports_position: Representative Ford (N & P) advanced this bill as local legislation specifically for Etowah County.
evidence_quotes: "This act shall apply only in Etowah County."
"A person who retired from the position of municipal police officer... and who resigned in good standing may be employed as a part-time school resource officer by Etowah County..."
"However, a part-time school resource officer shall not be required to meet physical examination requirements."
